items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Martial Solal... was leading a trio at the Ringside and they accompanied me... I really enjoyed playing with Martial

ctx.x: The morning of the 9th, the Flandre stopped at Plymouth, arrived at Le Havre around 7 that evening. We had a terrible weather, the boat was shaking like a nut shell and in spite of that we didn't get sea sick, we were glad to set foot on earth. We arrived in Paris at 10 that night. We had enjoyed a wonderful 70 days holiday, including the trip on the Liberte and the Flandre but were happy to get back to our regular routine of living again.

One month later, the 9th of July, I started work as an attraction at the Ringside which was a club on rue d'Artois, near the Champs Elysees, owned by an american Negro named Dick Edwards. Martial Solal, the great French pianist was leading a trio at the Ringside and they accompanied me and a girl singer, also Negro from the States, named Pat Boone.
